bull_bear.body:
- One of the largest Local Service Providers in the Government of Rajasthan's e-Mitra programme, with e-Mitra kiosks present in all 41 districts of Rajasthan
- Installed base of 8,499 active e-Mitra kiosks across Rajasthan, giving state-wide last-mile citizen-service reach
- Demonstrated system-integrator capability across fibre optic network deployment, FTTH, smart city and surveillance, and e-Governance infrastructure projects
- Strategic tie-up with a Reliance group company for an IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution being deployed in multiple Indian cities
- FTTH last-mile network in Rajasthan executed with BSNL and Railtel, with an achieved base of 18,000 customers
- Tie-ups with leading IT hardware OEMs (LG, Samsung, Acer, Dell, HP) supporting participation in government hardware procurement bids
- Vertically relevant product pairing — FRP rods are a strength member input into optical fibre cables, the Company's own other manufactured product
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Insolvency proceeding admitted against the Company under the IBC — A Financial Creditor's Section 7 application over a claim the Company disputes led the NCLT Jaipur Bench to admit the Company into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process and appoint an Interim Resolution Professional; the NCLAT has since directed the IRP to take no further steps while the Company continues under his supervision. The matter is unresolved and is a direct threat to control and going-concern status.
- Working capital and counterparty risk from telecom operator financial stress — The industry is exposed to working capital and counterparty risk primarily due to the financial stress of telecom operators; sector receivable cycles typically run 90-150 days and payment delays can strain liquidity and increase reliance on external borrowings.
- Dependence on telecom operator and government capital expenditure cycles — A substantial portion of demand is tied to telecom operators' capex cycles and government-funded projects, so deferment, slowdown or reprioritisation of such investment translates directly into demand variability. This is amplified for Aksh because its Services business is anchored on a Rajasthan state e-Governance programme and on BSNL/Railtel FTTH work.
- Right-of-Way, approval and project-execution constraints — Delays in obtaining Right-of-Way permissions, project clearances and infrastructure deployment approvals can extend timelines and escalate costs, causing cost overruns and deferred revenue realisation that affect project viability.
- Intensified competition and margin compression — Large global manufacturers alongside regional players have heightened competition, often producing aggressive pricing and margin compression, with sustained oversupply conditions capable of worsening this.
- Raw material cost volatility with limited supplier concentration — Fluctuations in key input prices including silica and petrochemical derivatives may adversely affect cost structures and profitability, a risk accentuated by limited supplier concentration.
- Technological substitution of fibre in last-mile connectivity — Although described as moderate, emerging technologies such as 5G Fixed Wireless Access, satellite-based broadband and evolving wireless standards may partially substitute fibre deployment in select last-mile use cases.
- Regulatory and policy change in import duties, localisation and public procurement — Changes in government policy on import duties, localisation norms or public procurement can impact competitiveness and supply chain dynamics — material given the share of the Company's order flow that comes from government tenders.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Aksh Optifibre makes optical fibre cable and Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) rods used as strength members inside optical fibre cables, selling into telecom, power transmission and infrastructure customers in India and overseas. Its Services business acts as a Local Service Provider in the Government of Rajasthan's e-Mitra programme delivering G2C and B2C citizen services through ICT-enabled kiosks, executes FTTH last-mile rollouts in Rajasthan with BSNL and Railtel, builds smart-city and smart-metering solutions, and functions as a system integrator and IT hardware supplier on government tenders. The Company states it operates in two segments viz. Manufacturing and Services.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Manufacturing:** Optical fibre cable, FRP (Fibre Reinforced Polymer) rods
- **Services:** e-Mitra ICT-enabled kiosks (e-Governance Local Service Provider), Mini e-Mitra (mobile e-Mitra), FTTH / broadband last-mile services, Smart solutions (smart water metering, smart dashboard, smart lighting, smart parking, solar inverter, smart level sensors), Turnkey projects / system integration (fibre optic network deployment, smart city and surveillance, e-Governance infrastructure), IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution, IT hardware supply

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Grow the e-Governance Local Service Provider business in Rajasthan's e-Mitra programme, having extended kiosk presence to all 41 districts after the state's district-boundary redefinition, and target 12.48% market share in both kiosk count and transaction count this year
- Launch and scale a mobile e-Mitra format called mini e-Mitra, targeting 5,000 mini e-Mitra units
- Expand the FTTH broadband business in Rajasthan — executed with BSNL and Railtel on a last-mile network with an 18,000 customer base — into additional areas and customer segments
- Build out the system-integrator / turnkey projects franchise across fibre optic network deployment, FTTH, smart city and surveillance, e-Governance infrastructure and collaboration solutions
- Deploy an IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution in multiple Indian cities through a strategic tie-up with a Reliance group company
- Develop smart solutions capability — smart water metering (prepaid and postpaid), smart dashboards and data analytics integrating smart lighting, smart parking, solar inverter and smart level sensors
- Pursue government IT hardware procurement tenders and turnkey IT projects on the back of OEM tie-ups with LG, Samsung, Acer, Dell and HP
- Diversify FRP end-use beyond telecom into power transmission, renewable energy and infrastructure applications
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The bundle contains no capex or capacity-addition programme for Aksh Optifibre — there is no commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking or new-plant narrative anywhere in the routed MD&A, Directors' Report or Corporate Overview text. What expansion intent exists is service-side and asset-light: the Company says it has started the mobile e-Mitra format called mini e-Mitra and is targeting 5,000 mini e-Mitra units, has taken e-Mitra kiosks into all 41 Rajasthan districts after the state redefined district boundaries (8,499 active kiosks) and is targeting 12.48% market share in both kiosk and transaction terms this year, and plans to further expand its FTTH broadband services in Rajasthan (executed with BSNL and Railtel, 18,000 customers achieved) into additional areas and customer segments. It is also deploying an IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution in different Indian cities through a strategic tie-up with a Reliance group company. Context for the absence of a capex programme: the Company reports a Nil CSR obligation on account of losses, recommended no dividend, and is the subject of an NCLT-admitted Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process in which the NCLAT has directed the Interim Resolution Professional to take no further steps while the Company runs under his supervision.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global fibre optic cable market estimated at approximately USD 11.5 billion in 2026 and projected to grow at a CAGR of around 6-7% over the medium term, supported by large-scale fibre deployment across telecom networks, data centers and smart city infrastructure
- AI-driven data center demand has emerged as the dominant growth catalyst in the current year, with hyperscalers and cloud providers raising optical connectivity investment — producing supply constraints and sharp increases in fibre prices due to limited upstream manufacturing capacity and long production cycles
- Telecommunications remains the largest demand segment, with over 65% of global fibre usage linked to telecom infrastructure, driven by 5G rollouts, FTTH expansion and broadband penetration
- Asia-Pacific continues to dominate the market, with India expected to grow at a higher CAGR of nearly 10% over the forecast period on digital infrastructure and rural connectivity investment
- The fibre optic cable industry is transitioning from a traditional telecom-driven cycle to a broader digital infrastructure backbone, with AI, cloud computing and data-centric ecosystems emerging as key demand drivers
- Government-led digital infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet are expected to drive large-scale fibre deployment and act as a sustained demand catalyst, particularly in rural and underserved areas
- FRP demand is supported by telecom (FRP rods as strength members in optical fibre cables amid 5G rollout and FTTH expansion) plus rising pull from power transmission, renewable energy and infrastructure projects; the business reflects stable growth with diversified applications
- India E-Governance Market projected to grow at a CAGR of 17.93% during 2025-2035 and the India Interactive Kiosk Market at 11.1%-15.95% up to 2034, underpinning the e-Mitra services business
- India Broadband Services Market projected to grow at approximately 15.6% CAGR up to 2033 on digital adoption, fibre broadband penetration, 5G rollout, OTT consumption and BharatNet / Digital India
- India IT Hardware Market projected to grow at approximately 7%-7.3% CAGR up to 2033 on digital transformation, e-governance, smart city projects, data center expansion and rising public-sector hardware procurement
- Offsetting pressures management flags: intensified competition and oversupply driving aggressive pricing and margin compression, raw material cost volatility (silica and petrochemical derivatives) with limited supplier concentration, dependence on telecom operator and government capex cycles, FX exposure from imported inputs and export-oriented operations, and execution delays from Right-of-Way and approval bottlenecks

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aksh Optifibre Limited is a Rajasthan-headquartered optical fibre cable and FRP rod manufacturer that also runs an ICT services business spanning e-Governance kiosks, FTTH, smart solutions, turnkey system integration and IT hardware, operating in two segments viz. Manufacturing and Services.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aksh Optifibre makes optical fibre cable and Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) rods used as strength members inside optical fibre cables, selling into telecom, power transmission and infrastructure customers in India and overseas. Its Services business acts as a Local Service Provider in the Government of Rajasthan's e-Mitra programme delivering G2C and B2C citizen services through ICT-enabled kiosks, executes FTTH last-mile rollouts in Rajasthan with BSNL and Railtel, builds smart-city and smart-metering solutions, and functions as a system integrator and IT hardware supplier on government tenders. The Company states it operates in two segments viz. Manufacturing and Services.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Aksh Composites Private Limited — subsidiary: Indian Wholly Owned Subsidiary (formerly known as Unitape Mandovi Composites Pvt. Ltd.); acquired August 17, 2010; reporting period March 31, 2026; reporting currency INR
- AOL FZE — subsidiary: Overseas Wholly Owned Subsidiary incorporated in SAIF Zone, Sharjah (U.A.E.), also referred to as Dubai in the related-party note; acquired August 21, 2017; holds the China step-down subsidiary; reporting currency AED
- AOL Technologies FZE — subsidiary: Overseas Wholly Owned Subsidiary incorporated in JAFZA, UAE (Dubai); acquired October 5, 2017; reporting currency AED
- Aksh Technologies (Mauritius) Limited — subsidiary: Overseas Wholly Owned Subsidiary incorporated in Mauritius; acquired July 18, 2017; reporting currency MUR
- AOL Composites (Jiangsu) Co. Ltd — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary incorporated in China, held through AOL-FZE, UAE; acquired September 15, 2016; reporting currency RMB
- MKC Industries Private Limited — related party: Enterprise over which KMPs and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence (Ind AS 24 related-party note)
- Mr. Aditya Katyal — related party: Relative of the Chairman, listed under KMP and their relatives in the Ind AS 24 related-party note

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Manufacturing:** Optical fibre cable, FRP (Fibre Reinforced Polymer) rods
- **Services:** e-Mitra ICT-enabled kiosks (e-Governance Local Service Provider), Mini e-Mitra (mobile e-Mitra), FTTH / broadband last-mile services, Smart solutions (smart water metering, smart dashboard, smart lighting, smart parking, solar inverter, smart level sensors), Turnkey projects / system integration (fibre optic network deployment, smart city and surveillance, e-Governance infrastructure), IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution, IT hardware supply

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Telecom operators and government-funded telecom programmes (BharatNet, Digital India)
- Government of Rajasthan e-Governance (e-Mitra citizen services)
- BSNL and Railtel FTTH rollouts in Rajasthan
- Power transmission, renewable energy and infrastructure projects (FRP)
- Smart cities / municipal smart infrastructure in India
- Government departments and public sector organisations (IT hardware procurement tenders)
- Within India (majority of revenue by customer location)
- Outside India / exports

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global fibre optic cable market estimated at approximately USD 11.5 billion in 2026 and projected to grow at a CAGR of around 6-7% over the medium term, supported by large-scale fibre deployment across telecom networks, data centers and smart city infrastructure
- AI-driven data center demand has emerged as the dominant growth catalyst in the current year, with hyperscalers and cloud providers raising optical connectivity investment — producing supply constraints and sharp increases in fibre prices due to limited upstream manufacturing capacity and long production cycles
- Telecommunications remains the largest demand segment, with over 65% of global fibre usage linked to telecom infrastructure, driven by 5G rollouts, FTTH expansion and broadband penetration
- Asia-Pacific continues to dominate the market, with India expected to grow at a higher CAGR of nearly 10% over the forecast period on digital infrastructure and rural connectivity investment
- The fibre optic cable industry is transitioning from a traditional telecom-driven cycle to a broader digital infrastructure backbone, with AI, cloud computing and data-centric ecosystems emerging as key demand drivers
- Government-led digital infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet are expected to drive large-scale fibre deployment and act as a sustained demand catalyst, particularly in rural and underserved areas
- FRP demand is supported by telecom (FRP rods as strength members in optical fibre cables amid 5G rollout and FTTH expansion) plus rising pull from power transmission, renewable energy and infrastructure projects; the business reflects stable growth with diversified applications
- India E-Governance Market projected to grow at a CAGR of 17.93% during 2025-2035 and the India Interactive Kiosk Market at 11.1%-15.95% up to 2034, underpinning the e-Mitra services business
- India Broadband Services Market projected to grow at approximately 15.6% CAGR up to 2033 on digital adoption, fibre broadband penetration, 5G rollout, OTT consumption and BharatNet / Digital India
- India IT Hardware Market projected to grow at approximately 7%-7.3% CAGR up to 2033 on digital transformation, e-governance, smart city projects, data center expansion and rising public-sector hardware procurement
- Offsetting pressures management flags: intensified competition and oversupply driving aggressive pricing and margin compression, raw material cost volatility (silica and petrochemical derivatives) with limited supplier concentration, dependence on telecom operator and government capex cycles, FX exposure from imported inputs and export-oriented operations, and execution delays from Right-of-Way and approval bottlenecks

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Grow the e-Governance Local Service Provider business in Rajasthan's e-Mitra programme, having extended kiosk presence to all 41 districts after the state's district-boundary redefinition, and target 12.48% market share in both kiosk count and transaction count this year
- Launch and scale a mobile e-Mitra format called mini e-Mitra, targeting 5,000 mini e-Mitra units
- Expand the FTTH broadband business in Rajasthan — executed with BSNL and Railtel on a last-mile network with an 18,000 customer base — into additional areas and customer segments
- Build out the system-integrator / turnkey projects franchise across fibre optic network deployment, FTTH, smart city and surveillance, e-Governance infrastructure and collaboration solutions
- Deploy an IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution in multiple Indian cities through a strategic tie-up with a Reliance group company
- Develop smart solutions capability — smart water metering (prepaid and postpaid), smart dashboards and data analytics integrating smart lighting, smart parking, solar inverter and smart level sensors
- Pursue government IT hardware procurement tenders and turnkey IT projects on the back of OEM tie-ups with LG, Samsung, Acer, Dell and HP
- Diversify FRP end-use beyond telecom into power transmission, renewable energy and infrastructure applications

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The bundle contains no capex or capacity-addition programme for Aksh Optifibre — there is no commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking or new-plant narrative anywhere in the routed MD&A, Directors' Report or Corporate Overview text. What expansion intent exists is service-side and asset-light: the Company says it has started the mobile e-Mitra format called mini e-Mitra and is targeting 5,000 mini e-Mitra units, has taken e-Mitra kiosks into all 41 Rajasthan districts after the state redefined district boundaries (8,499 active kiosks) and is targeting 12.48% market share in both kiosk and transaction terms this year, and plans to further expand its FTTH broadband services in Rajasthan (executed with BSNL and Railtel, 18,000 customers achieved) into additional areas and customer segments. It is also deploying an IoT-based CCMS smart panel solution in different Indian cities through a strategic tie-up with a Reliance group company. Context for the absence of a capex programme: the Company reports a Nil CSR obligation on account of losses, recommended no dividend, and is the subject of an NCLT-admitted Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process in which the NCLAT has directed the Interim Resolution Professional to take no further steps while the Company runs under his supervision.

- Vertically relevant product pairing — FRP rods are a strength member input into optical fibre cables, the Company's own other manufactured product
